data.body:
Change 3269 (Resolve fold lookups before the store lock) removes the clone-measured in-lock costs. It does not establish the production root cause, which stays pending until the next production sweep's timing log.

## Clone replay with the change (same 10 folds, same clone, warm caches)
- First fold: `attribution=12.34s signers=6.40s` now run before the lock; `held=0.78s` (was 11.8 s warm, 58.1 s cold).
- Folds 2-10: `held=0.43-0.69s`; `commit` is 0.41-0.76 s of each hold.
- No fold held the lock longer than 0.78 s, against the 60 s single-pass budget.

## Where the timing line lives
Each fold logs one WARNING line beginning `compaction fold timing: ticket=<id> outcome=<folded|skipped|error>`, followed by the 11 phase durations.
- Production's sweep runs in the async trigger's detached worker, at most once per `compact.trigger_interval_s` (default 6 h), started by a qualifying write. That worker's stderr is `compact-worker.log` in the `.rebar/logs/` directory beside the tracker. With `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, that is `/var/gerrit/site/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` inside the `rebar-mcp-<sha>-8093` container. Read it read-only with `docker exec <container> cat /var/gerrit/site/.rebar/logs/compact-worker.log` through an SSM `AWS-RunShellScript` payload.
- That path is in the container's own filesystem, not on a volume, so autodeploy's container replacement discards it. Read it after a sweep and before the next deploy. It was 0 bytes after the Nov 3 deploy; before this change the worker installed no log handler, so it would have stayed empty regardless.
- A sweep run inline (`compact.trigger = "always"`) or through `rebar store compact --all` logs the same line to that process's stderr (`journalctl` for the MCP container).

## Reading it
`held` is the whole locked span. If `held` is large and the named in-lock phases (`recover`..`commit`) sum to much less, the time went to work this line does not yet name, and the next check is to time inside that gap. `lock_wait` large means the fold itself queued behind another writer.
